ROLE: Decode a complete PUBLISH packet: DUP/QoS/RETAIN flags, a nonempty Topic Name without wildcards, a Packet Identifier exactly when QoS is 1 or 2, and an arbitrary binary payload.

SIGNATURE.RAW: enum wire_status wire_decode_publish(const uint8_t *packet, size_t len, struct wire_publish *out)
SIGNATURE.NAME: wire_decode_publish

STRUCT.NAME: struct wire_publish
STRUCT.ROLE: borrowed topic and payload slices plus the decoded flags

FUNC.NAME: wire_declared_body_len
FUNC.ROLE: confirm len is exactly the declared frame size

FUNC.NAME: wire_read_u16
FUNC.ROLE: read the topic name length prefix and the Packet Identifier

FUNC.NAME: topic_name_validate
FUNC.ROLE: require a nonempty UTF-8 topic name of at most 65535 bytes without 0x23 or 0x2B

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_declared_body_len
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: static enum wire_status wire_declared_body_len(const uint8_t *packet, size_t len, size_t *header_len, size_t *remaining_length)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: WIRE_COMPLETE with header_len (2..5) and remaining_length when len equals header_len + remaining_length
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: no ownership transfer; packet stays with the caller
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: any other result means the caller returns WIRE_INVALID without writing out

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: wire_read_u16
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the MSB-first 16-bit value at p (topic length or Packet Identifier)
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions (the caller checks that two bytes remain)

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: topic_name_validate
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: 1 when name is 1..65535 bytes of valid UTF-8 containing neither 0x23 ('#') nor 0x2B ('+'); 0 otherwise
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrows name for the duration of the call
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: 0 means the PUBLISH topic name is malformed, so this function returns WIRE_INVALID

LOGIC.INPUT: packet with len bytes holding exactly one framed PUBLISH (the caller obtained len from wire_decode_header.total_len); out receiving the flag bits and the borrowed topic and payload slices.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If packet is NULL or out is NULL return WIRE_INVALID. 2) Zero *out. 3) wire_declared_body_len(packet, len, &header_len, &rl): if it is not WIRE_COMPLETE return WIRE_INVALID. 4) Fixed header: if (packet[0] >> 4) != WIRE_PACKET_PUBLISH return WIRE_INVALID. flags = packet[0] & 0x0F; out->dup = (flags >> 3) & 0x01; qos = (flags >> 1) & 0x03; out->retain = flags & 0x01; out->qos = qos. 5) if qos == 3 return WIRE_INVALID (both QoS bits set is a malformed fixed header, MQTT-3.3.1-4). 6) if out->dup == 1 && qos == 0 return WIRE_INVALID (MQTT-3.3.1-2: DUP must be 0 for QoS 0 messages). 7) Topic Name: pos = header_len; require len - pos >= 2 else WIRE_INVALID; tlen = wire_read_u16(packet + pos); pos += 2; require tlen >= 1 (MQTT-4.7.3-1: a Topic Name must be at least one character) and pos + tlen <= len (topic runs past the packet) else WIRE_INVALID; if topic_name_validate(packet + pos, tlen) != 1 return WIRE_INVALID (ill-formed UTF-8, or a wildcard 0x23/0x2B in a Topic Name). out->topic = packet + pos; out->topic_len = tlen; pos += tlen. 8) Packet Identifier: if qos == 1 or qos == 2 require pos + 2 <= len else WIRE_INVALID; pid = wire_read_u16(packet + pos); if pid == 0 return WIRE_INVALID (MQTT-2.3.1-1); pos += 2. The identifier is validated then skipped: this broker routes only QoS 0 and closes a connection that sends QoS 1 or 2, so no identifier is retained in struct wire_publish. 9) out->payload_len = len - pos; out->payload = (out->payload_len == 0) ? NULL : packet + pos. A zero-length payload is legal and is reported as length 0 (never as a missing payload). 10) Return WIRE_COMPLETE. Topic and payload slices borrow packet verbatim; the payload is never scanned for NUL and is never treated as a C string.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: WIRE_COMPLETE with *out filled: topic/topic_len and payload/payload_len are borrowed slices of packet preserving the exact bytes (including 0x00 and an empty payload), dup/qos/retain carry the decoded flag bits. WIRE_INVALID for NULL arguments, a short or over-long frame, a reserved QoS value of 3, DUP set with QoS 0, a missing/empty/over-long/ill-formed topic name, a wildcard in the topic name, or a missing or zero Packet Identifier on a QoS 1/2 message. WIRE_INCOMPLETE is never returned. QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages are well-formed input that decodes successfully; refusing them is connection state policy applied by the broker.
INVARIANTS_USED: PUBLISH fixed header flags carry DUP (bit 3), QoS (bits 2-1) and RETAIN (bit 0)
QoS 3 is malformed and DUP must be 0 for QoS 0 (MQTT-3.3.1-2, MQTT-3.3.1-4)
a Topic Name is nonempty, valid UTF-8 and contains no wildcard (MQTT-4.7.3-1)
a Packet Identifier is present exactly for QoS 1 and 2 and is nonzero (MQTT-2.3.1-1)
the payload is arbitrary binary data whose length is carried by the frame, not by a terminator
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: packet holds one complete PUBLISH frame of len bytes, len >= 2.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: *out borrows bytes of packet; packet is neither modified nor copied and no allocation happens.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Pure function of its arguments; packet must not be mutated concurrently.

WIRE_MAPPING.RULE: stored verbatim; DUP=1 together with QoS 0 is WIRE_INVALID (MQTT-3.3.1-2). A DUP=1 QoS 1/2 message is decoded (the broker refuses QoS>0 by policy).
value 3 is WIRE_INVALID; 0, 1 and 2 are decoded, and only 0 is routable by this broker (scope R04).
stored verbatim for every QoS; this broker keeps no retained messages, so routing ignores the bit while a QoS 1/2 retain bit stays malformed only through the QoS rule.
length prefix bounded by the packet; length 0, ill-formed UTF-8 or a 0x23/0x2B byte is WIRE_INVALID (MQTT-4.7.3-1). Bytes are preserved exactly, with no normalisation and no lowercasing.

WIRE_MAPPING.WIRE_FIELD: Packet Identifier (present only when QoS is 1 or 2)
WIRE_MAPPING.RULE: must be present and nonzero for QoS 1/2 (MQTT-2.3.1-1) and must be absent for QoS 0; the value is not retained because QoS>0 messages are refused downstream.
arbitrary binary bytes including 0x00; an empty payload is legal and reported as length 0 with data NULL (scope R06).
